artworks.title: Hercules and Achelous
artworks.description: Louvre INV 536 from Reni's Mantuan Hercules cycle: the hero wrestles the river-god for Deianira — bull-form Achelous staged as monumental Baroque combat before the horn becomes cornucopia.

artworks.title: Deianeira watching Heracles fight Achelous (Attic column krater)
artworks.description: Louvre G365: Heracles seizes bull-bodied Achelous while Deianira looks on — the Calydonian contest that wins the bride and breaks the river's horn.

artworks.title: Achelous and Hercules
artworks.description: Smithsonian mural: Benton restages the river-god's bull-form wrestling with Heracles as American Regionalist energy — Deianira's suitor contest as modern mythic labour.

artworks.title: Hercules and Achelous
artworks.description: Dutch Mannerist oil: muscular Heracles locks with bull-horned Achelous — the Calydonian wrestling for Deianira as late-sixteenth-century figure painting.

popCulture.title: Deianira
popCulture.description: The bride Heracles wins from the river-god — Achelous' horn becomes the cornucopia of their wedding spoil.

popCulture.title: Achelous
popCulture.description: The shape-shifting river who wrestles Heracles for Deianira — bull, serpent, and man in one suitor.
